correctness.rationale: PASS: For complex operator-norm Schur multiplication, operator/nuclear duality gives ||S_M||=max_{p,q in simplex} ||diag(sqrt p) M diag(sqrt q)||_1. This is quantum fidelity between A=diag p and B=M diag q M^T and is jointly concave by the positive-matrix variational formula, allowing averaging over simultaneous GL(d,2) actions and transpose to p=q with two orbits {0} and nonzero characters. The reduced symmetric C has N−2 singular values sqrt N; its remaining 2D Gram eigenvalue sum simplifies to sqrt(t²+(4N−6)t+1). Thus F(t)=((N−2)sqrt N+sqrt(t²+(4N−6)t+1))/(t+N−1), whose unique t≥0 maximizer t_N=2sqrt(N(N+2))−(2N+1) gives boxed formula for N=2^d>=8. Expanding yields deficit N^-3/2+O(N^-7/2); row/column Walsh translations preserve norm of an arbitrary one-entry flip. Fresh independent numpy nuclear-SVD checks for N=8,16,32 recovered formula and optimizer to numerical precision, but global proof uses joint concavity and exact spectrum. Arbitrary asymmetric optimizers are not claimed to be unique.

originality.rationale: PASS (qualified): Holbrook–Johnston–Schoch show the general √N bound with equality precisely at genuine Hadamard matrices, and tabulate the order-four single-defect value, which is expressly not new. Davidson–Donsig transitive-symmetry norm formulas and Christensen's general self-adjoint variational representation describe broader frameworks but do not explicitly evaluate the nontransitive two-orbit one-flip Walsh family. The new contribution is the complete all-dyadic closed form, explicit optimizing weights and exact N^-3/2 loss. An earlier factorization or near-Hadamard perturbation formula remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed near-Hadamard, gamma-2 or operator-space factorization literature might have the same all-dyadic norm formula.
No uniqueness claim for arbitrary nonsymmetric maximizing p,q; only existence of the explicit two-level optimum and uniqueness within that reduced family.
Small numerical SVD checks cannot establish all dyadic orders, so global proof relies on concavity and Walsh spectrum identities.
